title: 4 Signs You’re Speaking From Hurt
paragraphs: And wounded words can sound righteous while quietly bleeding on everyone around you.

1. You always need the last word.
Not because truth matters.
Because pain wants control.
A bruised heart doesn’t just speak. It swings.
But “the anger of man does not produce the righteousness of God” (James 1:20).

2. You turn every disagreement into a personal attack.
Small correction. Big reaction.
Why? Because unresolved wounds make everything feel like rejection.
When the soul is raw, even gentle words can feel like knives.
“A gentle answer turns away wrath” (Proverbs 15:1).

3. Your words expose more bitterness than love.
Sarcasm. Shade. Cold truth without compassion.
You may be saying facts, but you’re no longer sounding like Jesus.
Because hurt loves to preach what it has not healed from.
And Scripture says, “Out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaks” (Matthew 12:34).

4. You speak to punish, not to restore.
That’s the dangerous one.
When pain becomes your pulpit, people stop hearing grace.
You don’t just want to be understood.
You want someone else to feel what you felt.

Jesus never asked us to fake healing.
He asked us to bring Him the wound.

Because unhealed pain will preach.
It will parent.
It will lead.
It will love.
And it will keep spilling into every conversation until grace touches the root.

The Gospel is not behavior management.
It is heart resurrection.

Christ doesn’t shame you for speaking from hurt.
He invites you to be healed from it.
Repent. Slow down. Let the Holy Spirit search your heart. Let Jesus cleanse what pain has poisoned.

You do not have to keep speaking from the place that broke you.
In Christ, you can speak from peace.
“Let no corrupting talk come out of your mouths, but only such as is good for building up…” (Ephesians 4:29)
